desc:
Monthly marketing campaign reports turn your ad, email and analytics numbers into a short document you will actually read. Ecom Swift LLC pulls the figures, explains them in plain words and lists the next steps worth taking.

## What is a marketing campaign report?

A marketing campaign report is a written summary of how your campaigns performed over a set period. It states what you spent, what you got back, which activities worked, which did not and what to change. A good report answers the question every owner asks: should I keep going, change something or stop?

It differs from a dashboard. A dashboard shows every number at once, while a report picks the few that matter and says what they mean.

## Why a plain report beats a dashboard

Most dashboards are built to show data, not to guide decisions. They hold dozens of charts, and busy owners stop looking at them. Months pass, a campaign quietly wastes budget and nobody notices until the bills add up.

A written report forces a conclusion. When someone explains why costs rose or why one email did better than another, you can act on it. This improves results indirectly: budget moves toward what works sooner, weak campaigns stop sooner and the next test is chosen on purpose. We cannot promise a particular result, since seasons, competition and your offer all play a part, but a regular report keeps decisions grounded in facts.

## What a good campaign report includes

- A summary at the top that tells you the main message in a few lines.
- Spend and results for each channel, shown side by side.
- Cost per result, so channels with different budgets can be compared fairly.
- A list of wins and misses, each with a short explanation.
- One simple chart per point, instead of a wall of graphs.
- Changes compared with the previous period, including what may have caused them.
- Notes on anything that distorts the numbers, such as a sale, a tracking gap or a site outage.
- Clear next steps in priority order.
- A short list of tests to run next.
- Plain English, with every term explained the first time it appears.

## How we produce your report

You give us viewer access to the tools you use, such as your ad accounts, email platform and analytics. Viewer access lets us read numbers but not change anything. If you prefer, you can send exported files or a spreadsheet instead.

We collect the figures, check them for gaps and use AI tools to spot patterns across channels. A person then reads the results, decides what is meaningful and writes the explanation. The Basic package covers one channel on a single page. Standard combines several channels, compares cost per result, shows changes from the previous month and ranks the actions. Premium covers more channels, compares two periods, adds a testing roadmap and budget suggestions and includes a walkthrough call.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide before the month starts what success looks like.
- Tell us about sales, price changes or site problems that affected results.
- Read the report with the people who control the budget.
- Pick two or three actions from the list, not all of them.
- Keep the same report layout each month so changes are easy to see.

**Avoid:**
- Judging a campaign on clicks alone when sales are what you want.
- Comparing months that had very different offers without noting it.
- Changing many settings at once, which makes the next report unreadable.
- Hiding bad results from the people who need to act on them.
- Sharing admin logins when viewer access is enough.

## Who these reports are for

This service suits an owner who runs ads and emails but has no time to read the data in each tool. It suits a small team that needs one report to share with a partner or investor. It also suits a business that hired a freelancer or agency and wants an independent view of what the numbers say.

## What we need from you

Tell us the period, the channels and your main goal. Add us as a viewer, analyst or read-only user on each tool where the platform offers that role, or send exports. We never ask for a password. If something looks wrong in the data, we say so in the report and explain what we could not verify.
